extracted.intended_audience: state agency rulemakers, administrative attorneys, and regulated persons (including small businesses and interested members of the public)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements governing notice, development, adoption, emergency action, incorporation by reference, hearings, cost analysis, and filing for administrative rules in Florida under the Administrative Procedure Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that rulemaking is practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking shall be presumed practicable unless the agency proves that: (a) the agency has not had sufficient time to acquire the knowledge and experience reasonably necessary to address a statement by rulemaking; or (b) related matters are not sufficiently resolved to enable the agency to address a statement by rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking practicability for fair notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking is presumed practicable to the extent necessary to provide fair notice to affected persons of relevant procedures and applicable principles/criteria/standards unless the agency proves that (a) required detail or precision is not reasonable under the circumstances, or (b) the particular questions are of such narrow scope that specific resolution is impractical outside adjudication based on individual substantial circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day notice of rule development after legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Legislature enacts a law requiring implementation by agency rules, the agency must publish a notice of rule development in the Florida Administrative Register within 30 days after the effective date of that law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory provisions not delayed by lack of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: No statutory provision shall be delayed in its implementation pending an agency’s adoption of implementing rules unless there is an express statutory provision prohibiting its application until the adoption of implementing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Least-cost alternative requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In adopting rules, agencies must, among alternative approaches to any regulatory objective and to the extent allowed by law, choose the alternative that does not impose regulatory costs on regulated persons, counties, or cities which could be reduced by adoption of less costly alternatives that substantially accomplish statutory objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: No inherent rulemaking authority or penalty power
rubrics_metrics.description: No agency has inherent rulemaking authority, nor authority to establish penalties for violation of a rule unless the Legislature specifically provides that the penalty applies to rules when establishing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules prior to statute effective; prohibition on retroactive rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may adopt rules authorized by law and necessary to implement a statute prior to the statute's effective date, but rules may not be effective until the statute is effective. An agency may not adopt retroactive rules unless expressly authorized by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-subject rule requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rule adopted shall contain only one subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicially noticed materials and parties' access
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may recognize materials that may be judicially noticed and may provide that such materials be incorporated into the record; before the record is completed, all parties shall be provided a list of these materials and given a reasonable opportunity to examine them and offer written comments or written rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference limited to materials as adopted
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule may incorporate material by reference but only as the material exists on the date the rule is adopted; for the purposes of the rule, changes in the material are not effective unless the rule is amended to incorporate the changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of another agency rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency rule that incorporates by specific reference another rule of that agency automatically incorporates subsequent amendments to the referenced rule unless a contrary intent is clearly indicated in the referencing rule; a notice of amendments to an incorporated rule must explain the effect on referencing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission and public access for incorporated materials (post-2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: In rules adopted after Dec. 31, 2010, or reviewed pursuant to s. 120.5435, material may not be incorporated by reference unless: (a) the material has been submitted in the prescribed electronic format to the Department of State and the full text can be made available for free public access via an electronic hyperlink from the rule in the Florida Administrative Code; or (b) posting would violate federal copyright law, in which case a statement to that effect and addresses where the material is available must be included in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic, text-searchable requirement for incorporated materials (post-2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: In rules proposed after July 1, 2025, material may not be incorporated by reference unless: (a) material submitted in prescribed electronic format to Dept. of State and the full text, in a text-searchable format, can be made available for free public access via an electronic hyperlink from the rule in the Florida Administrative Register; or (b) copyright exception with required statement and addresses included in notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments cannot be by reference only
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule may not be amended by reference only; amendments must set out the amended rule in full in the same manner as required by the State Constitution for laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special incorporation procedure for DEP/water management rules (ch.373 part IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a DEP or water management district rule is incorporated by reference in another agency’s rule to implement part IV of chapter 373, subsequent amendments to the incorporated rule are not effective as to the incorporating rule unless the incorporating agency notifies the committee and Dept. of State of intent to adopt the amendment, publishes notice in the Florida Administrative Register, and files the amended rule with Dept. of State; changes are effective 20 days after publication/filing; affected persons have 14 days to file objections specifying portions and reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency cannot adopt the objected portions in response to the objection; must publish notice of objection and its action in next available FAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding updates to agency-created incorporated documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency updates or changes a document it created that is incorporated by reference, the update or change must be coded by underlining new text and striking through deleted text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of State rulemaking for incorporation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of State may adopt by rule requirements for incorporating materials pursuant to the incorporation-by-reference provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing of rules in Florida Administrative Code
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule published in the Florida Administrative Code must be indexed by the Department of State within 90 days after the rule is filed; the Department shall establish procedures for indexing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation limits for agency heads
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency head may delegate authority to initiate rule development; however, certain rulemaking responsibilities (subparagraphs (3)(a)1., (3)(e)1., and (3)(e)6.) may not be delegated or transferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of rule development content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Except when repealing a rule, agencies must provide notice of the development of proposed rules by publishing a notice of rule development in the Florida Administrative Register at least 7 days before providing notice of a proposed rule. The notice must: (a) indicate the subject area to be addressed; (b) provide a short, plain explanation of the purpose and effect; (c) cite the grant of rulemaking authority and law being implemented; (d) include proposed rule number and, if available, preliminary text or a statement how to promptly obtain, without cost, any preliminary draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe to publish proposed rule after notice of development
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of a proposed rule must be published in the Florida Administrative Register within 180 days after the most recent notice of rule development, unless the Legislature provides a different date. The agency may exceed the timeframe only by submitting to the committee, at least 7 business days before the end of the 180-day period, a concise statement of reasons for delay and updating the statement quarterly until a notice of proposed rule is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readable language drafting standard
rubrics_metrics.description: All rules should be drafted in readable language: avoiding obscure words and unnecessarily long or complicated constructions, and avoiding unnecessary technical or specialized language understood only by particular trades or professions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public workshops for rule development
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may hold public workshops for rule development or information gathering for a statement of estimated regulatory costs. The agency must hold workshops (including regional workshops) for rule development if requested in writing by any affected person, unless the agency head explains in writing why a workshop is unnecessary. The explanation is not final agency action and failure to provide it when required may be a material error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For workshops/hearings, those responsible for preparing the proposed rule and SEC must be available to explain the proposal and respond to questions; workshops may be facilitated/mediated; notice of workshop must be published in FAR at least 14 days before and indicate subject area, contact, place, date, and time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiated rulemaking considerations and openness
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may use negotiated rulemaking and should consider it when rules are complex or strong opposition is anticipated. Consider whether a balanced committee of interested persons can be assembled, agency support provided, and whether group consensus can form the basis for a proposed rule. Notices must list representative groups invited; the negotiating committee must be noticed and open to the public and chaired by a neutral facilitator/mediator. Selection decisions and applications to participate are not agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of notice of intended action (adoption/amendment/repeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before adoption/amendment/repeal (other than emergency rules), upon approval of the agency head, the notice of intended action must include: (a) a short, plain explanation of purpose and effect; (b) the proposed rule number; (c) the full text of the proposed rule or amendment and a summary; (d) reference to grant of rulemaking authority; (e) reference to statutes being implemented or interpreted; (f) name, e-mail, and telephone of agency contact; (g) a concise summary of agency's statement of estimated regulatory costs (SEC) in readable language, if prepared; (h) agency website address where SEC can be viewed in full; (i) statement that persons wishing to provide information on SEC or proposals for lower-cost alternatives must do so in writing within 21 days after publication; (j) statement whether proposed rule is expected to require legislative ratification; (k) description of procedure for requesting a public hearing; (l) reference to date/place where notice of rule development appeared (except for repeals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice timing, availability, and delivery requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must be published in the FAR at least 7 days after the notice of rule development and at least 28 days before the intended action. The proposed rule, including all material proposed to be incorporated by reference, must be available for inspection and copying at time of publication. Material proposed to be incorporated must be made available per the incorporation rules. The notice must be mailed or delivered electronically to all persons named in the proposed rule and to persons who requested advance notice at least 14 days before publication; agencies shall also give notice to particular classes of persons as prescribed by rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing with committee before adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: The adopting agency shall file with the committee at least 21 days before the proposed adoption date: a copy of each proposed rule; a copy of any material incorporated by reference; a detailed written statement of facts and circumstances justifying the proposed rule; a copy of any SEC prepared; a statement of the extent to which the proposed rule relates to federal standards or rules on the same subject; and the notice required by the notice-content provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of correction for omitted/incorrect information
rubrics_metrics.description: If any required information in the notice (other than substantive changes to rule text) is omitted or incorrect, the agency must publish a notice of correction in the FAR at least 7 days before the intended action. Publication of a notice of correction does not affect timeframes for filing the rule for adoption. Technical changes must be published as a notice of correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of estimated regulatory costs (SEC) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency is encouraged to prepare a SEC before adoption/amendment/repeal, but must prepare a SEC if: (a) the proposed rule will have an adverse impact on small business; or (b) the proposed rule is likely to directly or indirectly increase regulatory costs in excess of $200,000 in the aggregate in the state within 1 year after implementation. The agency must make available any information used to determine whether the proposed rule meets these factors and include such information in the rulemaking record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency must consider factors outlined in s.120.541(2) but is not required to estimate the proposed rule's impact to those factors as part of the determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of impacts on small businesses, counties, and cities
rubrics_metrics.description: Before adoption/amendment/repeal, each agency shall consider the impact of the rule on small businesses (per s. 288.703) and on small counties/small cities (per s.120.52). Whenever practicable, an agency shall tier its rules to reduce disproportionate impacts and consider methods to reduce impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods to consider include: (I) establishing less stringent compliance or reporting requirements; (II) establishing less stringent schedules or deadlines; (III) consolidating or simplifying compliance/reporting requirements; (IV) establishing performance standards or best management practices instead of design/operational standards; (V) exempting small entities from any or all requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules ombudsman notice and alternative adoption process
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency determines the proposed action will affect small businesses, the agency shall send written notice of the rule to the rules ombudsman in the Executive Office of the Governor at least 28 days before intended action. The ombudsman may offer regulatory alternatives within 21 days; the agency shall adopt feasible alternatives consistent with objectives and that reduce impact. If alternatives are offered, the 90-day filing period is extended 21 days. The agency must provide the committee a copy of any regulatory alternative within 7 days after delivery. If the agency does not adopt all alternatives offered, it must file a detailed written statement with the committee explaining reasons before adoption and send a copy to the ombudsman within 3 working days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing request window and hearing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the intended action concerns any rule other than one relating exclusively to procedure or practice, the agency shall, on request of any affected person received within 21 days after publication of the notice of intended agency action, give affected persons an opportunity to present evidence and argument. The agency may schedule a public hearing and, if requested by any affected person, shall schedule one. When a public hearing is held, staff must be available to explain the proposal and respond to questions; boards must conduct at least one hearing themselves if hearings are requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any material submitted within 21 days after publication or submitted between publication and the end of the final hearing must be considered and made part of the rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to separate adjudicatory proceeding if rulemaking inadequate
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking proceedings are governed solely by these provisions unless a person timely asserts that their substantial interests will be affected and demonstrates that the proceeding does not provide adequate opportunity to protect those interests. If the agency determines the proceeding is inadequate, it must suspend the rulemaking and convene a separate proceeding under ss. 120.569 and 120.57; similarly situated persons may be requested to join; upon conclusion, rulemaking resumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice-of-change and support for non-technical changes
rubrics_metrics.description: After the final public hearing or after the time for requesting a hearing has expired, if the proposed rule has not been changed or contains only technical changes, the adopting agency must file a notice to that effect with the committee at least 7 days before filing for adoption. Any change other than a technical change must be supported by the record of hearings, be in response to timely written material submitted, or be in response to a proposed committee objection. Any non-technical change to an SEC requires a notice of change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any non-technical change to proposed rule text or incorporated material requires providing a copy of the notice of change by certified mail or actual delivery to any person who requests it within 21 days after the initial notice; agency must file the notice of change with the committee along with reasons, provide notice to requesters, at least 21 days before filing the rule. Notice of change must be published in FAR at least 21 days before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal for failure to meet timeframes or statements
rubrics_metrics.description: After the notice required by paragraph (a), the agency may withdraw the proposed rule in whole or part. The agency must withdraw the proposed rule if it has failed to adopt it within prescribed timeframes in the chapter or failed to submit the concise statement required under subparagraph (2)(a)2. If the agency fails to withdraw after committee notice, the Dept. of State must publish a notice of withdrawal; within 30 days after withdrawal, the agency must initiate rulemaking again if the mandatory grant of rulemaking authority is still in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on modification/withdrawal after adoption but before effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: After adoption and before the rule becomes effective, a rule may be modified or withdrawn only when: (a) the committee objects to the rule; (b) a final nonappealable order is entered in a rule challenge under s. 120.56 after adoption but before effectiveness; (c) when ratification required and Legislature does not ratify; (d) when the committee notifies the agency that an objection is being considered, the rule may be modified to extend the effective date by not more than 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of withdrawal/modification and post-effective amendment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall give notice of its decision to withdraw or modify a rule in the first available issue of the publication in which the original notice was published, shall notify persons described in prior notice-delivery provisions, and must notify the Dept. of State if the rule is required to be filed. After a rule has become effective, it may be repealed or amended only through the rulemaking procedures specified in this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee reporting of agency failures to file proposed rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee must, within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter, compile and post on its website a list of each failure by an agency to file a notice of proposed rule within the prescribed timeframe; the list must include agency name, website address where the notice of rule development may be found, citation to grant of rulemaking authority, timing metrics since filings, and a copy of the agency's concise statement required under subparagraph (2)(a)2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing for final adoption: materials and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: If the adopting agency is required to publish its rules in the Florida Administrative Code, the agency must electronically file with the Dept. of State a certified copy of the rule; one copy of any material incorporated by reference, certified by the agency; a summary of the rule; a summary of hearings; and a detailed written statement of facts and circumstances justifying the rule. Agencies not required to publish must file certified copy and other material in the office of the agency head open to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing restrictions for filing rule for adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule may not be filed for adoption less than 28 days or more than 90 days after the notice required by paragraph (a), subject to other waits (21 days after notice of change, 14 days after final public hearing, 21 days after SEC provided to persons with lower-cost proposals, or until administrative law judge decision), whichever applies. Extensions: if notice of change published before expiration, filing period extended to 45 days after publication; if public hearing notice published before expiration, filing period extended to 45 days after adjournment or related receipt dates; petition for administrative determination extends period to 60 days after final order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency certification and committee certification at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time a rule is filed, the agency shall certify that time limitations and statutory rulemaking requirements have been complied with, and that no administrative determination is pending on the rule. At the time of filing, the committee shall certify whether the agency has responded in writing to all material and timely written comments or inquiries made on behalf of the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department shall reject any rule not filed within prescribed time limits; not complying with statutory requirements or Department rules; upon which the agency has not responded in writing to all material/timely inquiries or comments; upon which an administrative determination is pending; or which does not include an SEC if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption effective date and tolling when committee review pending
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed rule is adopted upon being filed with the Dept. of State and becomes effective 20 days after being filed, on a later date specified in the notice, on a date required by statute, or upon ratification by the Legislature if required. Rules not required to be filed become effective when adopted by the agency head or later date specified. If the committee notifies an agency that an objection is being considered, the agency may postpone adoption to accommodate committee review; when postponed, the 90-day filing period is tolled until the committee notifies completion of its review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rule authority and required procedural protections
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency finds immediate danger to public health, safety, or welfare requires emergency action (or the Legislature authorizes and finds conditions met), the agency may adopt any rule necessitated by the immediate danger using any procedure fair under the circumstances if: (1) the procedure provides at least the procedural protection given by other statutes, the State Constitution, or U.S. Constitution; (2) the agency takes only that action necessary to protect the public interest; (3) the agency publishes in writing at the time of or prior to action the specific facts and reasons for finding immediate danger and reasons procedure used is fair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of emergency rules (except for educational units or single-county local units) including full text and agency findings must be published in the first available issue of the FAR and provided to the committee along with any incorporated material. Agency findings of immediate danger, necessity, and procedural fairness are judicially reviewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope examples for emergency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency rules pertaining to public health, safety, or welfare include rules pertaining to perishable agricultural commodities or the interpretation/implementation of certain election code chapters (97-102 and 105).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration, renewal, and replacement limits for emergency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An emergency rule may not be effective longer than 90 days and may not be renewable, except when the agency has initiated rulemaking to adopt rules addressing the subject and either: (a) a challenge to the proposed rules has been filed and remains pending; or (b) the proposed rules are awaiting ratification by the Legislature. If the proposed rule is not ratified, the emergency rule expires at adjournment sine die; the proposed rule must be withdrawn from ratification accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency may adopt identical rules through normal rulemaking procedures. Notice of renewal must be published before expiration and state facts/reasons. Emergency rules must be published in the Florida Administrative Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superseding and technical change rules for emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may supersede an emergency rule by adopting another emergency rule before the superseded rule expires; reason must be stated and the superseding rule may not be in effect longer than the duration of the superseded rule. Technical changes to an emergency rule are permitted within the first 7 days after adoption and must be published in the FAR as a notice of correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate effectiveness and early repeal of emergency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to applicable constitutional and statutory provisions, an emergency rule becomes effective immediately on filing (or on a date less than 20 days thereafter if specified) if the adopting agency finds such effective date is necessary because of immediate danger. An agency may repeal an emergency rule before it expires by providing notice in the FAR that includes full text and summary of the emergency rule and a short, plain explanation why the emergency conditions no longer require the rule.
